A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECHO study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary Sections 6–10 are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on BEHAVE, OMOMO, and AMASS, alongside ablations, conditioning tests, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results for two-stage training and quantitative physical plausibility in supplementary Tables S2–S3.

M1.justification: The proposed ECHO representations, tri-variate diffusion architecture, joint training, losses, contact guidance, and smooth inpainting remain unchanged. A-FT is an added experimental control using the same architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use BEHAVE, OMOMO, and AMASS and show Aria Digital Twin generalization. The added analyses use existing datasets and tasks; newly cited datasets do not expand the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: New Table S2 introduces ECHO A-FT as a training-strategy comparator, using AMASS pretraining followed by HOI fine-tuning. BoDiffusion+O and EgoAllo+H+O remain the external baselines; newly discussed related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds the two-stage training control and evaluates minimum human-object distance, contact percentage, penetration depth, and penetration score. The existing experiments retain their splits, preprocessing, training settings, and inference procedures.

E4.justification: Two focused supplementary analyses extend the existing suite: joint versus sequential training, beyond v2's NoAMASS ablation, and quantitative contact/penetration analysis. Existing component ablations, missing-tracking tests, and conditioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe the main comparisons as reporting mean and variance across three runs and use ± reporting. The added tables continue that convention without introducing new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and v2 Tables S2–S4, retained as v3 Tables S4–S6, are unchanged. New results include A-FT's AMASS MPJPE of 15.9±0.7 cm and physical-plausibility measurements. On BEHAVE, ECHO has 79.5% contact versus BoDiffusion+O's 54.0%, while BoDiffusion+O has lower penetration score, 0.021 versus 0.037 cm.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations, diffusion objectives, losses, guidance, inpainting equations, and existing metric definitions are retained. The new physical metrics are introduced as empirical evaluation measures without new formal derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the principal capability and performance claims. The introduction strengthens the novelty claim by explicitly stating that existing HOI methods cannot simultaneously learn motion priors and interaction dynamics from these data sources within one framework.

C2.justification: v3 attributes A-FT's degradation to the joint/tri-variate formulation rather than data access and explains BoDiffusion+O's lower BEHAVE penetration score through insufficient contact and floating objects. These are new interpretations; the limitations discussion is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code and trained-model release. v3 states that both are available and supplies repository and project-page links. The existing implementation details and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of IMU-HOI, I’M HOI, Glove2Hand, and other works, with fourteen additional references. It also sharpens distinctions from TriDi and the AMASS-prior strategies of InterDreamer and HOI-Diff while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the introduction and related work, accompanied by grammatical corrections, clearer runtime wording, and affiliation and acknowledgment updates. The main section order and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Tables S2–S3 and renumbers the former S2–S4 as S4–S6. Figure 1 labels explicitly identify three-point tracking alongside sparse conditioning; retained figures and tables are resized or relocated without changing their underlying qualitative examples.

improvement.justification: The new training control and contact/penetration measurements provide more direct evidence for claims previously supported by v2's existing ablations and qualitative comparisons. Expanded related-work distinctions and access information also help. The gain is limited: the same-architecture A-FT control supports joint training more directly than it isolates the tri-variate formulation itself, making the accompanying causal interpretation too strong.
